examples.en: I cut the paper with scissors.
Could you lend me your scissors?
Where are the scissors?
Please put the scissors back in place after you use them.
These scissors are too big.
At the salon they cut my hair with scissors.

explain: 영어 scissors와 달리 한 개로 세요. '가위 하나', '가위 두 개'처럼 말해요. 도구로 쓸 때는 '가위로 자르다'처럼 '로'와 함께 쓰고, 가위질하는 것은 '가위질'이라고 해요.

phrases.nuance_en: Used with '로' to name the tool.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is good at cutting with scissors.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the act of cutting with scissors.

phrases.example: 책상 위에 가위 두 개가 있어요.
phrases.en: There are two pairs of scissors on the desk.

explain_en: Unlike English 'scissors', it is counted as one item: '가위 하나', '가위 두 개'. As a tool it goes with '로' (가위로 자르다), and the act of cutting with scissors is called '가위질'.

examples.en: The two brothers look a lot alike.
This puppy looks just like a little bear.
They’re twins, but their faces look completely different.

examples.ko: 이 과일은 생김새가 특이해서 처음에는 못 먹을 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: This fruit has such an unusual shape that at first I thought it wasn’t edible.

examples.ko: 잃어버린 강아지는 생김새가 어때요? — 갈색이고 귀가 길어요.
examples.en: What does the lost puppy look like? — It’s brown and has long ears.

explain: ‘생김새’는 얼굴뿐 아니라 동물과 물건의 모양에도 써요. ‘잘생겼다’는 ‘생김새가 좋다’는 뜻이에요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 생김새 is not only for faces; it also works for animals and objects. 잘생겼다 means “good-looking,” literally that the 생김새 turned out well.

examples.en: This trip is for fifteen days.
My cold didn't get better for two whole weeks.
The parcel arrived after fifteen days.
I'm moving to a new home in half a month.
It has been fifteen days since I started my diet.

explain: '보름'은 열다섯 날이라는 순우리말이에요. 음력 십오 일, 달이 가장 둥근 날도 '보름'이라고 해요. 그래서 '보름달'이에요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The drought has continued for more than half a month.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 보름 가까이 질질 끌던 포로 교환 협상이 오늘 드디어 결실을 보았다.
dict_examples.en: The prisoner exchange talks, which dragged on for nearly two weeks, finally bore fruit today.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 보름 is a native Korean word for fifteen days. It is also the 15th of the lunar month, when the moon is fullest, which is why a full moon is 보름달.

examples.en: I laid small stones in the garden.

examples.ko: 겨울에 너무 추워서 정원의 나무가 죽었어요.
examples.en: It was so cold in winter that the trees in the garden died.

examples.ko: 우리 집 정원에는 장미가 많이 피었어요.
examples.en: Lots of roses have bloomed in our garden.
Tending a garden is my hobby.
We had a barbecue in the garden on the weekend.
I want to live in a house with a big garden.

explain: '정원'은 꽃과 나무를 보기 좋게 꾸민 곳이고 '마당'은 집 앞뒤의 빈 땅이에요. 정원은 '가꾸다'와 잘 어울려요. '정원 초과'의 '정원'(定員)은 소리만 같은 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: My grandmother tends the garden every morning.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb that goes best with 'jeongwon'.

phrases.en: Our school has a large garden.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the size of a garden.

phrases.en: All the flowers in the garden bloomed beautifully.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '의' to talk about things in the garden.

explain_en: '정원' is a place decorated with flowers and trees, while '마당' is the open yard around a house. It pairs well with '가꾸다' (to tend). The '정원' (定員, capacity) in '정원 초과' is a different word that just sounds the same.

examples.en: A strong wind blew and my umbrella flipped inside out.

examples.ko: 강풍 때문에 간판이 떨어질 수 있으니 건물 가까이 가지 마세요.
examples.en: Signs can fall in this strong wind, so don't go near the buildings.

examples.ko: 강풍 특보가 내려져서 바닷가 놀이공원이 문을 닫았습니다.
examples.en: A strong wind warning was issued, so the seaside amusement park closed.

examples.ko: 산 정상에는 강풍이 불어서 모자를 잡고 걸어야 했어요.
examples.en: A gale was blowing at the summit, so I had to walk holding on to my hat.

examples.ko: 어제 강풍에 베란다 화분이 떨어져서 깨졌어요.
examples.en: Yesterday a flowerpot on my balcony fell in the strong wind and broke.

explain: 바람과는 '불다'를 써요. 강풍이 불다, 처럼요. 비는 '내리다/오다'예요. 돌풍은 갑자기 부는 센 바람이에요.
explain_en: Wind takes the verb 불다: 강풍이 불다. Rain takes 내리다/오다. A 돌풍 is a sudden, strong gust.
